Connect density, area, sampling, transformations, and covariance geometry.

## Part A · Worksheet (~40 min, pen and paper)

### Problem 1 — Density versus probability ⭐

For $X \sim Uniform(0,0.2)$, find the density and $P(0.05<X<0.08)$. Why may the density exceed one?

### Problem 2 — Exponential waiting ⭐

For rate $\lambda=2$, find $P(X>1)$ and $E[X]$.

### Problem 3 — Linear transformation ⭐

If $X \sim N(2,9)$ and $Y=3X-1$, find the mean and variance of $Y$.

### Problem 4 — Covariance ellipse ⭐⭐

For $\Sigma=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$, find ellipse axes and standard deviations.

### Problem 5 — Mahalanobis ⭐⭐

Compare squared Mahalanobis distances of $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$ under that covariance.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Solutions — open only after attempting everything

**1.** Density is $5$; probability is rectangle area $5(0.03)=0.15$. Density is probability per unit, not probability.

**2.** $P(X>1)=e^{-2} \approx 0.135$ (the survival function $e^{-\lambda x}$) and $E[X]=1/\lambda=1/2$.

**3.** $E[Y]=3(2)-1=5$ and $\operatorname{Var}(Y)=3^2 \operatorname{Var}(X)=81$ — shifting moves the mean only; scaling multiplies the variance by the square.

**4.** Eigenvectors are diagonal/anti-diagonal with eigenvalues $7,1$, so standard deviations are $\sqrt{7},1$.

**5.** They are $2/7$ and $2$ respectively; the low-variance direction makes deviations more unusual.
:::
